basis: decisions.md D6 (T5, the LP-stake class): the firm's 1999 table lists 'Biovest Partners, Medical investment partnership, Distributed', and its 2008 and 2012 pages file 'Biovest' under the firm's own 'Investment Partnerships' category (/investment/biovest.html), so the position is a partnership interest. The 2008 to 2013 pages attach a description and link of Biovest International, Inc. (OTCQB: BVTI), an unrelated operating company; no SEC filing from 2001 on puts Sutter Hill Ventures in Biovest International's filings, so the description reads as the web page's mix-up, not an identification of an SHV equity holding.

decisions.md D6 (T5, the LP-stake class): the firm's 2008 and 2012 pages file Chengwei Capital under its own 'Investment Partnerships' category (/investment/chengwei.html: 'Chengwei Ventures invests in early-stage technology companies in greater China'), and the 2013 page describes a fund whose portfolio 'includes over 20 companies'. SHV's position is an interest in a venture fund, not equity in an operating company; Len Baker is named beside it as the firm's contact.

decisions.md D6 and D1 (T5, the LP-stake class): Costanoa Venture Capital is Greg Sands's own venture firm from 2012 (external under D1). The firm's 2013 to 2016 lists carry it beside its companies, and the 2013 page describes it as an early stage investor in cloud-based services, linking costanoavc.com; the position is an interest in its fund, not an operating company.

Sale consideration (COLLECTION.md s1, Erik 2026-09-22; the Point Nine share-swap ruling of 2026-09-26): the firm's 2008 and 2012 pages list Curis with the merger text 'Curis, Inc. will be formed by leveraging the combined strengths of Creative BioMolecules, Ontogeny and Reprogenesis'. The firm's 1999 table (every investment since 1970) lists Ontogeny and neither of the other two, so SHV's Curis shares are the consideration for its Ontogeny shares in the July 2000 merger; no SEC filing from 2001 on names Sutter Hill Ventures in Curis's filings, so no new money followed. The investment is Ontogeny (its own row, ontogeny).

T3 and decisions.md D4 (a post-IPO position with no pre-IPO round): SHV's only Corixa position is the August 2002 private placement of Corixa common stock (7,332,562 shares at $6.13, led by InterWest Partners); Corixa's 8-K of 2002-08-13 carries the purchase agreement signed for Sutter Hill Ventures, A California Limited Partnership by Tench Coxe. Corixa had been public since its 1997 IPO, and the firm's own 1999 table of every investment since 1970 does not list it, so there was no venture round in a private company: a purchase of a public company's stock. The firm's 2008 to 2016 listing does not change the instrument.

note: Gigabit Ethernet switches, San Jose (EDGAR registrant address). Acquired by Nortel Networks on 2000-10-04 (Wikipedia; the firm's 2010 page: 'acquired by Nortel Networks'). Entry: the IPO prospectus (424B4, 1999-09-24), Related Party Transactions, shows Sutter Hill Ventures buying Series A preferred in 5/96 (3,896,103 shares as converted at $0.51, the same block as Matrix Partners), then Series B (5/97, $3.33), C (6/98, $4.67) and D (6/99, $5.67); Tench Coxe has been a director since May 1996. Wikipedia agrees: the initial venture investors were Matrix Partners and Sutter Hill Ventures.

Collaborative product-design software, Santa Clara (EDGAR registrant address). Listed by the firm only in 2004 (Software). Status aligned with sibling Benchmark (defunct, ceased operations after the 2001 bust); EDGAR shows a paper Form D as late as 2002-05-14 and nothing after, and Google News finds nothing. The round SHV joined is not on record.

Web services (SOA) management software, Oakland (EDGAR registrant address; paper Form Ds 2002 to 2008). Acquired by Oracle in 2010 (the firm's 2013 page: 'was acquired by Oracle'). The firm's 2004 page quotes the company as founded in 2001 with significant venture backing from Sutter Hill and Norwest, which puts SHV in at founding but names no round; no press or filing names it, so the stage is undetermined.

Urology implants, Minnetonka, Minnesota. The firm's 1999 table: 'Acquired by Pfizer' (sibling Greylock dates the sale 1985 from its own listing); aligned with Greylock on status and city. This is the original AMS, not the AMS Holdings later bought out of Pfizer. The round SHV joined is not on record (before EDGAR).

Medicaid managed care, Virginia Beach. Acquired by WellPoint (now Elevance Health) in 2012 for $4.9B (Wikipedia). Fund position confirmed by the 2001 S-1/A: the principal stockholders footnote 'Represents securities owned by Sutter Hill Ventures, a California Limited Partnership' and its Entrepreneurs Funds. The prospectus lists Series A, B and C convertible preferred (8,000,000, 7,025,000 and 6,480,000 shares), Series D issued to Prudential for its Medicaid business (1999) and Series E redeemable preferred ($5.0M each in July 1998 and January 1999), but it does not say which series SHV bought, so the stage is undetermined (sibling Accel's Series A is a model label).

Urine drug monitoring for pain medication, Baltimore, with its lab in Greensboro, NC. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ameritox): in 2018 it sold its book of business, auctioned its equipment and other assets and ceased to operate; an asset sale out of a wind-down reads acquired (COLLECTION.md s6). Aligned with sibling Bain Capital Ventures (acquired); sibling Sequoia still reads private, and the cited 2018 sale is fresher. The firm listed it 2008 to 2016 with Jeff Bird as managing director; no source names the round SHV joined.

Glucose self-testing devices, Scotts Valley, California (model knowledge). The firm's 1999 table lists it as private; its 2008 and 2013 pages: 'was acquired by Roche Diagnostics'. The round SHV joined is not on record.

Diabetes drugs (Symlin, Byetta), San Diego; founded 1987, IPO 1992 (Wikipedia). Acquired by Bristol-Myers Squibb in 2012 (tender offer filings on EDGAR from July 2012; the firm's 2013 page says so). The firm's 1999 table lists it as public; the round SHV joined is not on record (before EDGAR).

Engineering workstations, founded 1980 in Chelmsford, Massachusetts; acquired by Hewlett-Packard in 1989 for $476M (Wikipedia; the firm's own pages say the same). Aligned with sibling Greylock (acquired, US, Industrial & Robotics). The founding-era round SHV joined is not on record.

Network monitoring and consulting; the firm's 1999 table lists it as private and no later page carries it. Google News, EDGAR and the firm's archive give no fate and no location (the name now belongs to an unrelated UK pensions administrator), so status is unknown and the city unplaced; US is inferred from the firm's 1999 portfolio, which is US companies. The round SHV joined is not on record.

BIS anesthesia-depth monitors. Acquired by Covidien in 2009 for $210M (Wikipedia). Country disputed: the Wikidata IE reflects the later owners (Covidien, then Medtronic, both Irish-domiciled); Aspect was a Massachusetts company (Natick at its 1999 S-1, Norwood in its later EDGAR filings), hence US and Norwood. The S-1/A lists Series C (1997, $3.75 a share, about $12.9M), D (February 1998, $7.00) and E (December 1998, $10.00) but names no SHV purchase and SHV is not a 5% holder, so the round SHV joined is undetermined; the firm's 1999 table lists Aspect as private.

Avant! Corporation, IC design (EDA) software, Fremont (EDGAR registrant address). Merged into Synopsys on 2002-06-06 (Wikipedia, Synopsys; the firm's 2013 page: 'has been acquired by Synopsys'), so acquired and below_1b. Disputed prefill: the private 1b_plus mark ($1.98B, 2015, unicorn list) belongs to Avant, the Chicago online lender, a name match; sibling ribbit-capital's avant is that lender (a collision, not aligned). EDA reads Industrial & Robotics, as on the other books' EDA rows. The round SHV joined is not on record.

Digital video and audio editing, Burlington, Massachusetts. Taken private by an STG affiliate in November 2023 for $1.4B (Wikipedia), so acquired; aligned with siblings Greylock and Sequoia. The firm's 1999 table lists Avid (public) and, separately, Digidesign ('Acquired by Avid', 1995); the firm does not list its other stock-paying acquirers (Genzyme, EndoSonics, Nortel), which reads as a direct Avid position rather than Digidesign consideration, though no filing confirms either. The round SHV joined is not on record (IPO 1993, before EDGAR).

VINES network operating system, Westborough, Massachusetts (EDGAR registrant, renamed ePresence). Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banyan_VINES): the company dropped the Banyan name for ePresence in 1999, sold its services division to Unisys in late 2003 and liquidated its Switchboard holdings; an asset sale out of a wind-down reads acquired. Aligned with sibling Battery (acquired); sibling Greylock reads defunct on the liquidation. IPO 1992; the round SHV joined is not on record.

BÂRRX Medical, ablation therapy for Barrett's esophagus, Sunnyvale (EDGAR registrant address; paper Form Ds 2003 and 2004, an electronic one in 2010). Acquired by Covidien in January 2012 (the firm's 2013 page). No source found names the round SHV joined.

Skin and connective tissue repair, Cambridge, Massachusetts. The firm's 1999 table: 'Merged with Genzyme' (sibling Greylock's listing dates it 1995); aligned with Greylock (acquired, Cambridge). The round SHV joined is not on record.

User-generated talent-contest site (Bix.com Inc., earlier 900 Seconds Inc., Palo Alto per its EDGAR registration; paper Form Ds 2006 and 2007). Acquired by Yahoo in February 2007 (the firm's 2013 page). No source found names the round SHV joined.

Veterinary drugs, headquartered in Greensboro, NC; acquired by IDEXX Laboratories in October 1998 (the firm's own 2008 and 2013 pages; its 1999 table: 'Acquired by IDEXX'). The round SHV joined is not on record.

Company not identified. The firm listed 'Bonafide' in 2015 and 2016 with a logo only (no description or link), and its 2015 team page files it under Mike Speiser beside Pure Storage, Snowflake, Sumo Logic and Sila Nanotechnologies, so it reads as a stealth company of his. Tried: EDGAR (no issuer of that name with an SHV person; Bonafide Provisions LLC of Oceanside is a bone-broth maker whose Form D names no SHV person), Google News and web search (nothing). Country disputed: the Wikidata AR is Bonafide, an Argentine coffee brand, a wrong join on a one-word name; US is inferred from the Speiser listing. Stage, band and graduation read undetermined for an unnamed company.

Boxer, a mobile email and task client (Boxer Inc., Austin; Form D of 2013-10-15 at 701 Brazos, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1589031/000158903113000002/0001589031-13-000002-index.htm). Silicon Hills News (2013-10-22): a $3 million seed round led by Sutter Hill Ventures (the Form D: first sale 2013-10-02, $2,889,398 sold of $3,089,398); the predecessor TaskBox had raised $600,000 from angels. Sam Pullara (at SHV from 2012) is the firm's managing director for it. Acquired by VMware (AirWatch) in October 2015 (Data Center Dynamics). Country disputed: the Wikidata value belongs to another Boxer, a wrong join on a one-word name. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Bracket Computing, Mountain View, founded 2011 by Tom Gillis and Jason Lango (Wikipedia; VentureBeat). The firm's 2015 team page files it under Mike Speiser. SHV was in the October 2015 $46.4M round (VentureBeat; SiliconANGLE calls it the Series C) that brought total funding to $131.4M; the earlier rounds and SHV's entry are not named in any source found, so the stage is undetermined (sibling a16z's Series A is a model label). VMware took its IP and staff in May 2018 (Wikipedia); aligned with sibling a16z (acquired, US, Security).

Brierley+Partners, loyalty marketing and loyalty technology, founded 1985 by Hal Brierley, Dallas. Sold to Nomura Research Institute in 2015 (Dallas Innovates; Dallas Morning News, https://www.dallasnews.com/business/2015/03/31/dallas-brierley-partners-sold-it-s-the-firm-behind-big-rewards-programs/) and acquired by Capillary Technologies in April 2023 (Dallas Innovates; Business Wire). The firm listed it 2010 to 2016 under Business & Financial Services; the round and size of SHV's position are not on record.

Buzznet, music and pop-culture social network, Los Angeles; later Buzz Media and SpinMedia. Wikipedia: '$35 million in four rounds' by 2008 from Focus Ventures, Anthem, NEA, Redpoint and Sutter Hill Ventures; the round SHV joined is not named. SpinMedia sold Buzznet, Idolator and PureVolume to Hive Media in September 2016, an asset sale out of a wind-down, so acquired.

C3 Energy is C3.ai (NYSE: AI): founded 2009 by Thomas Siebel as C3, renamed C3 Energy, C3 IoT (2016) and C3.ai (2019), Redwood City (Wikipedia). Market cap $1.67B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), so 1b_plus. Fund position: Sutter Hill Ventures, A California Limited Partnership is a party to the registration rights agreement filed with the 2020 S-1 (exhibit 4.2, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1577526/000162828020016443/0001628280-20-016443-index.htm), and C3's January 2018 $100M release names Sutter Hill among existing investors. The firm listed it from 2013 with Jim White as managing director. The S-1 names no SHV purchase (its Series A converts into 21,000,000 Class B shares), so the round SHV entered is undetermined.
Cardiac measurement catheters, Mountain View (EDGAR registrant address; its public filings run 1996 to 1997). The firm's 1999 table: 'Acquired by Endosonics'. The round SHV joined is not on record.

Ceon, service fulfilment and product-lifecycle software for communications providers, Redwood City (EDGAR; paper Form Ds 2002 and 2003). Acquired by Convergys in October 2008 (Venture Capital Journal, 'Convergys Buys VC-Backed Ceon Corp.'; Light Reading). The firm's 1999 table lists it as private; the round SHV joined is not on record.

ClaimCard, payment cards and software for insurance claims, Sunrise, Florida; later renamed WildCard Systems, a prepaid card processor (PropertyandCasualty.com). SHV provided ClaimCard's $3.3 million second round in December 1998 as the only named investor; the source names no series and SHV's part in any first round is unknown, and a 'second round' does not collapse onto one stage, so the stage is undetermined. eFunds agreed to acquire WildCard Systems in June 2005 (Finextra, https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/13803/efunds-to-acquire-wildcard-systems), so acquired.

Budgeting and planning (performance management) software. Acquired by Lawson Software for about $4 million in October 2003 (The Register, https://www.theregister.com/on-prem/2003/09/30/lawson-swooping-in-on-closedloop/846818; the firm's 2004 and 2013 pages). The article and the firm's pages give no location and EDGAR has no filing under its name, so the city is unplaced. The round SHV joined is not on record.
T1 multiplexers; the firm's 1999 table: 'Acquired by DCA' (Digital Communications Associates), a deal before EDGAR. No source found gives its location or the round SHV joined.

Customer loyalty software and targeted marketing for retailers (the firm's 1999 line: 'Customer loyalty software'), Lisle, Illinois (EDGAR registrant address; paper Form Ds 2002 and 2005). A vendor profile (PitchBook) records its sale to DS-IQ, Inc. on 2010-04-14, consistent with the firm dropping it after 2012; no press confirmation found, so the sale rests on that profile. The round SHV joined is not on record.

Online advertising network for the US Hispanic market, San Francisco (EDGAR registrant address; paper Form Ds 2005 to 2007). Acquired by AudienceScience (the firm's 2013 page). No source found names the round SHV joined.

DSL access equipment, Palo Alto (EDGAR registrant address; operations in San Diego). IPO prospectus (424B4, 1999-05-13), Certain Transactions: in April 1996 the company sold 2,723,000 shares of Series A preferred at $1.00 under an agreement dated 1996-04-10, 1,250,000 of them to entities affiliated with Sutter Hill Ventures and 1,250,000 to Greylock; SHV also bought Series B ($3.39) in January 1997. Tench Coxe has been a director since March 1996, the company's inception. Acquired by Tut Systems in 2005 (merger proxy DEFM14A on EDGAR, April 2005); IPO'd then acquired reads acquired.

Cardiovascular drugs (Integrilin), South San Francisco (EDGAR registrant address). Merged into Millennium Pharmaceuticals in February 2002 (merger communications on EDGAR from December 2001; the firm's 2013 page: 'merged with Millenium Pharmaceuticals'). IPO 1991, before EDGAR; the firm's 2013 list names Len Baker as its managing director. The round SHV joined is not on record.

Cytel Corporation (cell adhesion drugs, San Diego) is the EDGAR registrant CIK 822206, renamed Epimmune in 1999 and IDM Pharma in 2005 (Irvine, California). Takeda bought IDM Pharma by tender offer in June 2009 (SC TO-T and 25-NSE filings), so acquired; the city is the registrant's last address. The round SHV joined is not on record (IPO before EDGAR).

Datis Corporation, databases and analyses for hospitals. HCIA acquired all of its capital stock on 1995-04-28 for $14,250,000 in cash (HCIA's 1996 prospectus, 424B4); the firm's 1999 table says 'Acquired by HCIA'. The prospectus gives no location for Datis, so the city is unplaced. The round SHV joined is not on record.

Digital audio workstations (Pro Tools), founded 1984 as Digidrums, Menlo Park (EDGAR registrant address). Acquired by Avid Technology in 1995 (Wikipedia; the firm's 1999 table: 'Acquired by Avid'). The round SHV joined is not on record.

Mobile and social games studio founded 2003 by Trip Hawkins, San Mateo (Wikipedia); closed in 2014 after selling its games to RockYou (status defunct as prefilled, aligned with sibling Sequoia). The firm listed it 2008 to 2016 with Jim White as managing director. A February 2011 Series D ($12M) is on record, but no source names the round SHV entered (its 2004 Form Ds are paper filings), so the stage is undetermined.

Ion chromatography and analytical instruments, Sunnyvale (Wikipedia). Thermo Fisher Scientific announced its acquisition for $2.1B in December 2010 (acquired, as prefilled). SHV's David Anderson was a director through the 2000s (Dionex proxy statements on EDGAR); the founding-era round SHV joined is not on record.

Agricultural e-commerce portal founded 1999. Acquired by AgriStar Global Networks in August 2001 and relaunched as AgriStar (trade press headline 'DirectAg acquired, relaunches as AgriStar'); headquarters Saint Paul, Minnesota per a vendor profile. The firm's 1999 table lists it as private; the round SHV joined is not on record.

Web affiliate network; the firm's 1999 table lists it as private and no later page carries it. Google News and web search find nothing on the company (the name collides with unrelated products), so status is unknown and the city unplaced; US is inferred from the firm's 1999 portfolio. The round SHV joined is not on record.
